# INTRODUCTION

Body text starts here. First-level headings (INTRODUCTION, METHODS,
RESULTS, DISCUSSION, CONCLUSIONS, ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS, REFERENCES) are
left-aligned and rendered in caps automatically by the Heading 1
style -- type them in normal sentence case if you prefer, e.g.
`# Introduction`.

Cite sources in APA7 author-date form, e.g. as shown by Smith and
Jones [@exampleCitation2024] or in parenthetical form
[@exampleCitation2024]. Multiple parenthetical citations are sorted
alphabetically and separated by semicolons automatically by the CSL
style.

Upon first mention of a species in the abstract and body text (and in
figure/table captions), give the English common name directly followed
by the scientific name, no parentheses or comma, e.g. Sooty Shearwater
*Ardenna grisea*. Italicize genus/species names; capitalize English
species names but not group names (e.g. "petrels").

# METHODS

## Statistical analysis

Second-level headings use sentence case (only the first word and
proper nouns capitalized) and stay left-aligned, e.g. "Statistical
analysis" above.

### Multivariate methods

Third-level headings are italic sentence case, e.g. "Multivariate
methods" above. Use third-level headings sparingly.

Report statistics with an indicator of variance and significance;
italicize statistical notation (*n*, *P*, *t*, *F*) by wrapping it in
asterisks, e.g. `*n*` and `*P*` render as *n* and *P*.

Include an ethics statement here if the study involved field work or
handling of live birds/eggs (institution name, permit numbers, animal
care committee certification).
